title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference customer-success and support guidance for enterprise onboarding: integration steps, the escalation matrix, known issues and workarounds, health check procedures, and QBR material to present to customers. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and Engineering on-call.

Scope

- Applies to all enterprise customers onboarding with Dedicated or Private deployments and high-volume Hosted API customers with a support SLA.
- Covers technical integration (API keys, routing, webhooks), production cutover checklist, triage and escalation flows, and recurring health-check/QBR artifacts.

Ownership and Contacts

- Document owner: customer-success (Aisha Patel)
- Primary teams: customer-success, solutions-engineering, eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime
- On-call aliases: #cs-oncall, #se-oncall, #infra-oncall (PagerDuty)

High-level Goals

1. Reduce time-to-first-successful-call to production for enterprise customers.
2. Provide clear SLAs and escalation steps so support handoffs are predictable.
3. Ensure QBRs are data-driven and focus on reliability, cost, and roadmap alignment.

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (before first integration call)

- Customer has an assigned CSM and SE.
- Security questionnaires reviewed (if required) and confidentiality level confirmed.
- Network readiness: IP allowlist information has been shared for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- API keys and test account created in staging environment.
- Integration runbook scheduled (60-120 minute technical session).

Integration Guide (technical)

1) API Authentication and Keys
- Provide the customer with a scoped API key for staging and a separate key for production.
- Keys are created via Console > Organizations > API Keys. Keys use least privilege: ingestion-only vs full-management.
- Rotation policy: rotate every 90 days for Dedicated/private customers; document rotation steps during handoff.

2) Endpoints and Regions
- Hosted API: https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate
- Dedicated: per-customer endpoint provided in onboarding email (e.g., https://dedicated-us-east-1.customer.redwood.internal)
- For Private (VPC/on-prem) follow the customer-specific routing instructions in the reference-architecture page.

3) Sample CURL test (staging)

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <STAGING_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://staging.api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"Hello","max_tokens":32}'

4) Webhooks and Callbacks
- Events: request.completed, request.failed, model.rollback
- Recommended retry policy on customer side: exponential backoff, start 1s, max 30s, 5 retries.
- Example webhook payload fields: request_id, status, duration_ms, tokens_consumed, model_version.

5) Configuration Recommendations

| Setting | Recommended Value | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Batch size | 8-16 (workload-dependent) | Balances throughput and p95 latency |
| KV cache TTL | 24 hours | Improves prefix reuse for chat workloads |
| Quantization profile | int8 or int8-gptq (if supported) | Cost savings with acceptable quality degradation for non-sensitive tasks |
| Warm-up traffic | 100-1500 requests over 30 min | Stabilizes JIT kernels and cache behavior |

Production Cutover Checklist (run during migration week)

1. Validate production API key and endpoint are reachable from customer's network.
2. Smoke test 20 sample requests; verify p95 latency and correctness.
3. Confirm monitoring ingestion: customer events are visible in Console > Integrations > Logs.
4. Enable canary rollout: route 5-10% traffic to production model variant for 24 hours.
5. Confirm billing/quotas are configured and customer understands thresholds and overage policy.

Escalation Matrix and Procedures

Severity definitions and SLAs (enterprise SLA example)

- P1 (Sev 1) — Production down or complete loss of inference for customer impacting all users.
  - Target response: 15 minutes (acknowledge)
  - Target engage: engineering on-call within 30 minutes
  - Resolution goal: restore service or implement documented mitigation within 4 hours

- P2 (Sev 2) — Significant functional degradation (high error rate, severe latency regression)
  - Target response: 1 hour
  - Engage: SE/infra within 2 hours
  - Resolution goal: 12-24 hours

- P3 (Sev 3) — Partial impact, single feature affected, or minor bugs
  - Target response: 4 business hours
  - Resolution goal: next normal release cadence (days to weeks)

Escalation steps (numbered procedure)

1. Triage by CS/Support: collect request_id, timestamps, example payloads, SDK version, region, model_version, and approximate traffic.
2. If P1 or P2, open PagerDuty incident with "Redwood Enterprise P{1|2}: <customer-name>" and tag teams: eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime, solutions-engineering.
3. Attach logs and latency/error metrics to the incident. Use Console > Traces and Logs to link evidence.
4. SE to attempt known-workaround (see Known Issues) while infra investigates root cause.
5. Communicate cadence to customer every 60 minutes for P1 and every 4 hours for P2.

Escalation Contacts (who to page)

- Level 1: #cs-oncall (CS triage)
- Level 2: #se-oncall (solutions engineering)
- Level 3: #infra-oncall / Eng SRE PagerDuty (production impact)
- Leadership notification: Customer Success Director and VP Eng for P1 incidents beyond 4 hours

Known Issues and Workarounds (operational table)

| Issue ID | Symptom | Root Cause (short) | Workaround | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KI-2026-01 | Elevated 500 errors for large-batch requests | Suboptimal kernel selection for long sequences on specific GPU drivers | Reduce batch size to 4 or enforce max_input_length=1024 until a runtime patch is released | eng-serving-runtime |
| KI-2026-02 | Memory growth on chat sessions after long-lived connections | KV cache TTL not purged due to client not closing sessions | Restart the model process or instruct client to rotate session_id and close inactive connections | eng-sre |
| KI-2026-03 | Webhook delivery retries spike causing duplicated events | Customer webhook endpoint returns 500 for bursts | Advise customer to implement idempotency keys and increase webhook ingestion capacity; use event batching on customer side | customer-success |

Each known issue entry above links to a deeper triage doc in eng-serving-runtime (use related_pages for links).

Health Checks and Monitoring (daily/weekly)

Daily Health Summary (automated):
- p95 inference latency (target: < 350 ms for < 16k tokens workloads)
- Error rate (5xx) per 100k requests (target: < 0.05%)
- Token throughput vs quota (alerts at 80% of committed capacity)
- KV cache hit rate (target: > 60%)
- Model fallback frequency (target: < 1% of requests)

Weekly Health Review (CS/SE):
- Customer usage trend (7d / 30d / 90d)
- Cost per 1k tokens and anomaly detection on spend
- Recent incidents and mean-time-to-resolve (MTTR)
- Open action items from previous QBR

QBR Template and Deliverables

Use the following sections when preparing the quarterly business review deck for the customer:

1) Executive summary: overall health, key wins, and risks.
2) Metrics: core SLOs, usage trends, cost breakdown (hosted/dedicated cost drivers).
3) Reliability review: incidents since last QBR, resolutions, and action plan.
4) Optimization opportunities: batching/quantization recommendations and estimated $ savings.
5) Roadmap alignment: upcoming product capabilities relevant to customer.
6) Action items and owners: clear owner and ETA for each item.

A sample QBR slide list is stored in /confluence/sales-enablement/pitch-decks/enterprise-qbr-template.

Routine Operational Playbooks (quick references)

- Rotate API keys for a customer: Console > Customers > <org> > Keys > Rotate; update customer and schedule maintenance window if Dedicated.
- Force model rollback to last known-good version: Eng SRE command: rwi rollback --customer <id> --service model-serve --version <vX.Y.Z>. Only Eng SRE or on-call SE may execute.
- Increase quota for Dedicated pool: submit Capacity Change request via eng-sre ticket queue with expected peak QPS, token profile, and time window.

Communication and Customer Updates

- For P1 incidents: provide an initial incident summary within 60 minutes, followed by status updates every 60 minutes until mitigation.
- For major configuration changes (routing, dedicated pool resize, quantization migration) provide a 72-hour notice and runbook.

Appendices

A. Example Integration JSON snippets

API call with function/tool-calling metadata (sample):
{
  "model":"redwood-13b",
  "input":"Summarize the following content...",
  "max_tokens":"256",
  "metadata":{ "customer_org":"acme-corp","request_type":"summarization" }
}

B. Escalation checklist (quick copy)

1. Gather: request_id, timestamps, region, model_version, SDK version.
2. Triaged: reproduce in staging? yes/no.
3. Mitigation applied: yes/no.
4. PagerDuty incident created: incident#

C. Useful Console locations

- Console > Organizations > <org> > Activity (requests, errors)
- Console > Integrations > Webhooks (delivery history)
- Console > Models > <model> > Versions (performance profile)
